## 🔴 Errors (likely broken or will cause build failures)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props:10–12` — `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `.props` is dead code (AP-21)

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (all projects in this repo), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The SDK's `TargetFramework` logic runs in the `.targets` import phase. This condition will never be true, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is silently never set.

**Fix:** Move this block into `Directory.Build.targets`:

```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets:6–10` — Property defaults in `.targets` override project-level settings

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` is imported **after** the project file. MSBuild uses last-write-wins semantics, so these values unconditionally override anything projects set. Concretely, `LibB.csproj` sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` on line 13, but this `.targets` file stomps it back to `true`. LibB's opt-out is silently ignored.

**Fix:** Move overridable defaults to `Directory.Build.props` and use conditional assignment:

```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

This lets individual projects override the defaults. Only use `.targets` for values that **must** be enforced and cannot be overridden.

---

### 3. `LibA.csproj:13` — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This replaces `DefineConstants` entirely, wiping out `DEBUG` and `TRACE` which the SDK defines by default. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working in Debug builds.

**Fix:** Append to the existing value:

```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 4. `LibA.csproj:13` — Unquoted `Condition` attribute

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** Both sides of the comparison are unquoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty or contains spaces, the condition will fail to evaluate or mismatch silently. This is a classic MSBuild pitfall.

**Fix:** Quote both sides:

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 5. `LibA.csproj:43–45` — Publish-on-build re-invokes the project via `<MSBuild>` task (self-referential build)

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** This forks a **second MSBuild evaluation** of the same project with an additional global property (`_IsPublishing=true`). The two instances share the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, creating a race condition where both instances write the same files concurrently. This can cause intermittent build failures, corrupted outputs, or "file in use" errors.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to invoke Publish in the **same** project instance, or add Publish as a post-build step externally (CI script). If you must keep it:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);PublishAfterBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="PublishAfterBuild" Condition="'$(_IsPublishing)' != 'true'">
  <!-- Run publish targets in-process -->
</Target>
```

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj:7–9` — F# file compilation order is wrong

<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />     <!-- defines types used by Services -->
